title: Fix rate-limit/quota header consistency across endpoints + add regression tests
author: Ethan Park
description:
Context: Support has multiple reports of confusing/incorrect rate-limit headers after SDK upgrades and during fallback routing (SUP-1843, SUP-1855). In particular: (1) some endpoints emitted RateLimit-* while others only emitted X-RateLimit-*; (2) reset values were inconsistently rounded (ms vs s); (3) quota-limit vs request-rate-limit were conflated, resulting in 429 responses with headers that suggested a long-term quota exhaustion when the user was simply bursting; (4) in a subset of fallback codepaths, we emitted headers computed from the upstream pool defaults instead of the customer/account plan, causing Remaining to jump between requests. This PR standardizes header emission across all public inference endpoints, splits "rate limit" vs "quota" semantics, and adds regression coverage for gateway + fallback paths.

What’s included: - Header standardization: Always emit IETF-style RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, RateLimit-Reset (seconds) on 200/4xx responses for chat/completions, embeddings, rerank, and legacy completions routes. - Back-compat: Continue emitting X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset for now (same values). Added a single codepath that computes both sets, so they can’t diverge. - Quota vs rate: Introduce Redwood-Quota-Limit and Redwood-Quota-Remaining (tokens/day for hosted plans; capacity units for Dedicated where applicable). These are intentionally separate from RateLimit-* (requests/min and tokens/min), and are omitted when unknown/unavailable (e.g., Private deployments with customer-managed policy). - 429 classification: Ensure the JSON error payload includes error.type in {"rate_limit_exceeded","quota_exceeded"} and set Retry-After consistently for rate-limit 429s. - Fallback path fix: When routing falls back to a compatible model/region, headers now reflect the customer/account limits (not the fallback pool defaults). Also adds a counter metric redwood.gateway.ratelimit.header_source{source=account|pool_default} to help debug mismatches.

Out of scope: changes to pricing/entitlements, UI changes in Console, or SDK behavior changes beyond consuming these headers.

Rollout notes: This is safe to ship as it’s additive. Existing headers are preserved with identical values. We can deprecate X-RateLimit-* once clients confirm RateLimit-* adoption (tracking in ENG-4825).
commits: gateway/ratelimit: compute headers via single builder and attach to all routes
gateway/errors: classify 429 as rate_limit_exceeded vs quota_exceeded; set Retry-After
routing/fallback: propagate account limit context into fallback execution path
tests: add integration coverage for headers across endpoints + fallback regression
metrics: add header_source metric and debug log guardrails
testing:
Unit: services/gateway/test/unit/ratelimit_headers_builder.spec.ts
Integration: services/gateway/test/integration/ratelimit_headers.spec.ts (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank) + services/gateway/test/integration/fallback_headers.spec.ts (fallback on capacity + fallback on model incompat)
Manual: hit /v1/chat/completions in staging with a low RPS plan and verify RateLimit-* and X-RateLimit-* match; verify 429 includes Retry-After and error.type

review_conversation:
Mina Haddad (2026-02-12): We should be explicit about units. Today X-RateLimit-Reset is sometimes ms in older clients. Are we *guaranteeing* seconds now? Also, can Remaining ever be negative? 

Ethan Park (2026-02-12): Good call. This PR guarantees RateLimit-Reset and X-RateLimit-Reset in seconds (integer, ceil to next second). Remaining is clamped at 0. Added comments + a unit test for clamping and rounding.

Sean Gallagher (2026-02-13): Please ensure we’re not emitting quota headers for Dedicated/Private in ways that imply contract terms. Also, Retry-After should only be set for rate-limit 429s (not quota) since quota exhaustion is not time-bound.

Ethan Park (2026-02-13): Updated: Redwood-Quota-* only emitted when we have a clear, time-bounded policy in the gateway (hosted plans). For Dedicated/Private, omit unless policy plugin provides it. Retry-After only for error.type=rate_limit_exceeded.

Dylan Brooks (2026-02-13): Tests look good. Request: add a regression that mimics SUP-1855 where fallback changes the header source. The fixture should assert header_source metric increments too (even if just via mock).

Ethan Park (2026-02-13): Added fallback_headers.spec.ts with a forced fallback path and asserted the header builder uses account context. Metric assertion added via test harness spy.

Mina Haddad (2026-02-14): One nit: The new Redwood-Quota-* naming should be consistent with existing Redwood-* headers (we have Redwood-Request-Id). Can we prefix with Redwood-Quota-* (already) and avoid X-Redwood-*? 

Ethan Park (2026-02-14): Done. No X-Redwood-* introduced.

Approvals: Mina Haddad approved (2026-02-14). Sean Gallagher approved (2026-02-14). Dylan Brooks approved (2026-02-14).
release_notes:
- Standardized rate-limit headers across chat/completions, embeddings, rerank, and legacy routes (RateLimit-* + X-RateLimit-*).
- 429 responses now clearly indicate rate_limit_exceeded vs quota_exceeded and set Retry-After when applicable.
- Fixed header inconsistencies during fallback routing; headers now reflect account limits.
